solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is received inside another

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
haste is a rush or hurry
one is I, and the 's is S

explanation.surface: A cold shower or an icy rush of air is being praised as a character-building discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as a possessive, but it splits into the letter for one plus the S of the apostrophe. 'Discipline' is a verb here, meaning punish.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise someone is to punish or rebuke them, which is one verb sense of discipline.

clue.text: Bad smell on a right pig!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another means it comes first, above the rest

blocks.note: BO is body odour
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the stink coming off a thoroughly piggish person is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A right pig' sounds like British slang for an awful person or mess, but 'right' is just R and the pig is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is an uncastrated male pig, or a wild pig, so it is a kind of the animal named.

clue.text: Small audio apparatus with small bone

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
tape is the recording medium of audio equipment, cassettes and reels
the same abbreviation again

explanation.surface: A description of a compact sound system, placed beside a tiny bone, like something in a museum case.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's audio theme is apt: the definition is a bone of the ear, so the sound picture hides the anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The stapes, or stirrup, in the middle ear is the smallest bone in the human body.

clue.text: Close second slipped catching first person

indicators.note: to catch something is to trap it within your grasp, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to slip up is to make a mistake, to err
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: the fielder standing close at second slip grabs the catch that dismisses the first batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket: 'close', 'second slip' and 'catching' are all fielding words. SERRIED is S plus ERRED with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Serried ranks stand pressed together, shoulder to shoulder, so the word describes things packed tightly.

clue.text: Explore excavation obtaining a large gem

indicators.note: to obtain something is to take possession of it, so it ends up held inside another piece

blocks.note: to tour a place is to travel round and explore it
a mine is a dug-out excavation
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An explorer digs at a site and turns up a big precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The mining scene makes the gem sound like a find rather than the definition; 'large' is the standard clothing-size abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourmaline is a crystalline silicate mineral cut and polished as a semi-precious stone in many colours.

indicators.note: a cleared room has had its contents taken out, so only the outermost letters survive
in a down clue, whatever sits under something else is placed after it

blocks.note: beet is a root vegetable
the word emptied of its inner letters

explanation.surface: A gardener clears away the grubs found beneath a vegetable crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect larvae' wants to be read together as grubs; in fact 'Insect' is the definition and 'larvae' is the word that gets emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect whose front wings have hardened into protective cases, the largest insect order.

clue.text: Restrict and almost confuse cycling Latvian

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
cycling means going round, so a letter moves from the front round to the back

blocks.note: to throw someone is to disconcert or confuse them
a Lett is a Latvian, an old name for the people

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone keeps limiting and bewildering a Latvian cyclist.
explanation.walkthrough: Lett is an old name for a Latvian, found mostly in crosswords. Cycling moves the front letter to the back without otherwise disturbing the order.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle is to choke off or limit, as a throttle restricts the fuel flow to an engine.

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
robed means clothed in a robe

explanation.surface: A doctor inspects a patient, who then puts their clothes back on without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quietly comes from musical notation, where piano means soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate or look into closely, so probed matches examined as a past tense verb.

clue.text: Puritan admits heartless evil is beginning

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is gone, leaving just the ends
to admit someone is to let them in, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: a prude is a prim, puritanical person
the word with its central letters removed

explanation.surface: A Puritan confesses that heartless wickedness is where all sin starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless evil' reads as cruelty; it actually trims evil to its outer letters, which go inside PRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelude is an introductory piece or event that comes first, so it is the opening of something.

indicators.note: nearly means not completely, so the last letter is lost
flipping something over turns it round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Rastafarians revere Haile Selassie, former emperor of Ethiopia

explanation.surface: A devotee of the Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie almost loses his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emperor Selassie' reads as one phrase, but 'Emperor' is the definition. RASTA loses its last letter and is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, so the title names a supreme imperial ruler.

clue.text: Do go on about Queen favourite

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps round others

blocks.note: to prate is to chatter on at length
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
the teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: Someone urges a speaker to keep talking about the Queen's favourite, perhaps a corgi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do go on' reads as polite encouragement, but 'Do' alone is the definition, in its sense of commit a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate is to carry out or commit, usually a crime, so it works as a verb meaning do.

blocks.note: first meaning: an old word for several or various
second meaning: those who dive into water

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is archaic, surviving in phrases like 'divers ways'; the question mark flags the plainer second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means various or sundry, while the noun names swimmers who leap head first into a pool.

indicators.note: being about something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter
comical means amusing
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Someone is spared by their darling, who finds a rejection amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as a lover, but it means the heart of the word 'sweet', a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Economical means careful not to waste, using no more than necessary, which is being sparing.

indicators.note: something following comes after, so that piece is placed second in the answer

blocks.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
to be behind schedule is to be late

explanation.surface: An instruction to trail along at the back after some bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow behind' reads as one phrase, but only 'Follow' is the definition, and 'behind' means late rather than at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to copy or imitate them, taking them as a model, a figurative sense of follow.

clue.text: Sweetheart left almost finished in sack

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes
being in something means sitting inside it, so these pieces go within another

blocks.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in 'hit the sack'
L is the abbreviation for left
over means ended or finished

explanation.surface: A lover is abandoned, nearly done for, after being fired from a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' suggests dismissal, but here it is slang for bed, as in 'hit the sack'. 'Almost' trims only the word for finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A beloved is the person someone loves dearly, a noun sense matching darling or lover.

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting letters up makes them read from the bottom upward, backwards

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I for the one
to mark something is to note it

explanation.surface: A pupil is cheered by a new top grade on his work.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a crossword staple for excellent, with the 1 standing in for I. ETONIAN is Eton College's pupil, a famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: An Etonian is a pupil at Eton College, the English boys' school, so the definition gives an example.

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold back within limits, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a deed is an act or action
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police's plainclothes detective branch

explanation.surface: A company takes legal steps to hold back undercover officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a business, but it is an adjective meaning resolute. The CID is Britain's detective branch, whose officers work out of uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A decided view is firm and definite, unwavering rather than hesitant, so both adjectives mean resolute.

indicators.note: to take something on is to take it aboard, so it goes inside the other piece

blocks.note: to entail is to require or involve
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Taking on a Republican opponent requires courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' reads as courage, the quality needed for the political fight; it is the anatomical sense instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrails are the intestines and inner organs of a body, which are literally the guts.

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and taking it away beheads the word

blocks.note: a function is a job or role

explanation.surface: Someone takes a lid off a tube in order to get at the ointment inside.
explanation.walkthrough: FUNCTION loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unction is anointing with oil, and by extension the oil or salve itself used for the purpose.

clue.text: One is he, she or they?

definitions.text: One is he, she or they?

blocks.clueFragment: One is he, she or they?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about someone's gender or identity
setter's reading: these three words are examples of a part of speech, and 'One' is another

explanation.walkthrough: The question sounds like asking whether a person is male, female or non-binary; the answer is the grammatical category that all these words belong to.
explanation.definitionFit: He, she and they are words standing in for a noun, and grammar calls such substitutes by this term.

clue.text: Fathers concerned with being in homes

indicators.note: being inside something means one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a pad is slang for someone's home
re means regarding or concerning

explanation.surface: Dads who are fixated on being at home with the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fathers' suggests parents, but here they are priests. Re is the memo word for concerning, and pad is slang for a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is a title for a priest or military chaplain, who is addressed as Father in the Church.

clue.text: Shut up keeping warmth in cover

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: sh is the hushing sound telling someone to be quiet
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hush and stay warm under a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' suggests being enclosed, but it is the command to be quiet, the two-letter hushing sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting protective case, like a scabbard for a blade, so it is a kind of covering.

blocks.note: first meaning: to check someone out thoroughly
second meaning: to broadcast a programme

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a TV programme about a veterinary surgeon; 'Vet' is a verb meaning to check.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates are screened when examined for suitability, and a film is screened when it is broadcast or shown.

indicators.note: to restrict is to confine within bounds, so the letters are enclosed by the surrounding words

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A small car out in front is racing badly, or keeps its engine running poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' looks like an anagram signal for mini's, but the answer sits inside aheAD MINIS TERribly.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer an organisation is to manage and direct it, which is to run it.

clue.text: Envelop with ribbons and paper, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word contributes only its opening letter

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Instructions for doing up a present using ribbon and wrapping paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The gift-wrapping scene is exactly the answer; 'and' supplies its A, so it is part of the wordplay rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something is to enfold or cover it completely, which is what envelop means.

blocks.note: first meaning: a river in north-east England flowing through Durham and Sunderland
second meaning: gradual damage by use or friction

explanation.surface: Water wearing away its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England; the two words read as one phrase about riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Wear and tear is gradual deterioration from use, the same slow wearing away as erosion.

indicators.note: something done occasionally happens only now and then, so just every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
the main is an old poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: Sailors must put up with a sea that turns vicious from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: The main for sea is a crossword convention from phrases like 'the Spanish Main'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to last or continue in existence, which is what it means to remain.

indicators.note: partially means in part, so only a section of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Work trousers that only half cover someone, and stink besides.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through cOVER ALL Smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are a bib-fronted work garment, and overalls is the general name for such protective clothing.
